page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5-c8g1.4xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine designed for high-compute and parallel processing workloads. Powered by the KVM hypervisor on an x86_64 architecture, this instance configuration provides 16 vCPUs (8 physical cores with 2 threads per core) driven by an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The CPU features 40 MB of L3 cache along with AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA instruction support. Memory capacity is provisioned at 120.0 GB of RAM, offering 7.5 GB per vCPU.

Hardware acceleration is supplied by two NVIDIA Pascal-generation P100 GPUs delivering a combined 32 GB of VRAM. For persistent local caching and rapid temporary data access, the instance bundles 944 GB of dedicated local SSD storage. Baseline networking throughput is capped at 5 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a clear divide between single-thread processing and multi-threaded throughput. Single-core stress-ng performance scores at 954.09, falling into the bottom 10% tier, while single-threaded gzip compression (21.45 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (7.87 GB/sec) both demonstrate weak results. In contrast, multi-core stress-ng reaches 9532.02 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression scales to 59.76 GB/sec, placing overall multi-threaded CPU handling in the middle tier. Memory benchmarks record 56.56 GB/sec for uncached read-only streams and 31.42 GB/sec for write throughput. In-memory operations via Redis yield 10.88 million SET operations per second, complemented by a static web serving throughput of 9.91 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.gn5-c8g1.4xlarge centers on its legacy CPU microarchitecture and modest single-core execution speed relative to its substantial parallel capacity. Cost efficiency remains favorable for workloads that predominantly leverage the dual NVIDIA P100 GPUs, generous memory allocation, and local SSD space rather than aggressive single-threaded CPU processing. Best-fit use cases include parallel scientific computing, GPU-based batch data processing, machine learning training workflows compatible with Pascal architecture, and high-memory computational modeling.
